Subject: Follow-up: Prompt collection + model fit next steps

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we don’t lose momentum:

- Goal: Validate model fit for Acme’s customer support summarization and triage assistant.
- Scope: ~200 representative prompts from your live transcripts (edge cases + typical flows).
- Success criteria: F1/precision on entity extraction > 0.88 and no major quality regressions across your top 10 critical prompts.

Recommended immediate next steps (from our side):
1) Prompt collection: Please fill the attached prompt_collection_template.csv with ~200 prompts (columns: id, prompt_text, expected_behavior, edge_case_flag, pii_flag). Include a few redaction examples for any prompts that contain customer PII.
2) Benchmark link: We’ll run a 1k-token benchmark and share results — see our model fit benchmarks here: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/2026/q1-model-fit
3) Model recommendations: Start with redwood-llama-3-small for fast iteration and redwood-optimize-1 for production checks. If you need lower-cost inference we can test a quantized variant (q4_0).
4) Quality monitoring: We’ll set up prompt-level regression alerts tied to your prompt set; please highlight any prompts that are business-critical.

Attachments: prompt_collection_template.csv (CSV template)

Can you confirm who on your team will own populating the CSV and whether there are any strict redaction/retention constraints (legal/security)? If helpful we can host a short working session to walk through the template.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Ownership: Sarah (cc’d) will lead the prompt collection, but legal will need to sign off on any PII examples we send.
- Redaction: Can you confirm what level of redaction you prefer? We typically redact email addresses and account IDs but want to understand if you need full hashes or redacted placeholders.
- Retention: Our security team requests that any customer data provided for benchmarking be deleted from vendor systems after 90 days and that we receive an audit log of access.

Also, curious about the model recs — you mentioned redwood-llama-3-small and redwood-optimize-1. Do you have a short summary of tradeoffs (latency vs. quality) and a link to any recent benchmarks?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Prompt collection + model fit next steps

Hi Tom / Sarah —

Thanks — noted on ownership and legal. Quick answers below and next actions.

Redaction & retention:
- For prompt collection please send 2 sets: (1) production-style prompts with redacted placeholders (e.g., <EMAIL_REDACTED>, <ACCOUNT_ID>) and (2) a small set (<=20) of non-production examples that include real PII for us to validate redaction heuristics. We will:
  - Use placeholders for the bulk of the dataset.
  - Treat non-production PII examples as sensitive: we’ll ingest them into a short-lived, access-restricted enclave, run the checks, and delete within 30 days by default (we can match your 90-day requirement if you prefer).
  - Provide an audit log of who accessed the enclave.

Model tradeoffs + benchmarks:
- redwood-llama-3-small: lowest cost and fastest for iteration; good for initial fit and surfacing edge-case failures. Latency typically 50-120ms/token on Dedicated in our benchmarks; quality is strong on conversational prompts but may miss subtle entity linkages.
- redwood-optimize-1: production-grade, better entity accuracy and stability for structured outputs; higher cost but fewer regressions. Latency ~80-180ms/token depending on QPS and sequence length.
- Quantized variants (q4_0): cost savings ~30-45% with small degradation on very long-context logic.

Benchmarks: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/2026/q1-model-fit (same link as above) — I’ve attached our Q1 PDF summary for quick read.

Quality regression monitoring:
- We’ll register your prompt set and wire up per-prompt alerts. If a new model rollout causes >5% relative drop on a critical prompt, we’ll send an incident and rollback plan.

Next actions:
1) Sarah: please populate prompt_collection_template.csv and upload to the secure folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-redwood-acme (or reply with attachments).
2) Legal/security: do you want us to sign a DPA addendum for the short-lived enclave? We can route that through your procurement team.
3) I’ll queue a 60-min workshop with our model ops engineer to review your uploaded prompts and sample runs — suggested slots below.

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-2026-q1.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
